transformer.name: Transformer
transformer.definition: A transformer transfers energy through magnetic coupling between windings. It can raise or lower an alternating voltage, or provide electrical isolation between circuits.
transformer.caption: A simplified outdoor power transformer: insulated terminals above, a tank and cooling surfaces below.
transformer.svg: <svg viewBox="0 0 250 180" role="img" aria-label="A simplified outdoor power transformer: insulated terminals above, a tank and cooling surfaces below." xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg"><g fill="none" stroke="#5d7450" stroke-width="1.4" stroke-linecap="round" stroke-linejoin="round"><rect x="74" y="62" width="95" height="70" rx="2" fill="#e5e9d9"/><rect x="80" y="68" width="16" height="57" rx="2" /><line x1="104" y1="69" x2="104" y2="125" /><line x1="113" y1="69" x2="113" y2="125" /><line x1="122" y1="69" x2="122" y2="125" /><line x1="131" y1="69" x2="131" y2="125" /><line x1="140" y1="69" x2="140" y2="125" /><line x1="149" y1="69" x2="149" y2="125" /><path d="M69 133H176M81 133V144M162 133V144M93 62V45M123 62V40M151 62V45" /><path d="M87 47h12m-12 5h12m-12 5h12" /><path d="M117 47h12m-12 5h12m-12 5h12" /><path d="M145 47h12m-12 5h12m-12 5h12" /><path d="M169 85H183V112H169M65 100H74" /></g><style>text{fill:#748263;stroke:none;font:8px ui-monospace,monospace;letter-spacing:1px}</style></svg>

transmission.name: Transmission
transmission.definition: Transmission networks move bulk electrical power between generators, regions, and major substations. For a given power transfer, using higher voltage reduces current and resistive losses. Transmission can use AC or DC, with overhead lines or underground cables.
transmission.caption: Overhead transmission conductors hang from insulator strings on a steel lattice tower.
transmission.svg: <svg viewBox="0 0 250 180" role="img" aria-label="Overhead transmission conductors hang from insulator strings on a steel lattice tower." xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg"><g fill="none" stroke="#5d7450" stroke-width="1.4" stroke-linecap="round" stroke-linejoin="round"><path d="M102 148 124 36 146 148M109 112H139M115 82H133M120 58H128M102 148 139 112 115 82 128 58M146 148 109 112 133 82 120 58" /><path d="M88 64H160L138 52H110ZM78 91H170L143 78H105Z" /><line x1="94" y1="64" x2="94" y2="78" /><line x1="154" y1="64" x2="154" y2="78" /><line x1="84" y1="91" x2="84" y2="105" /><line x1="164" y1="91" x2="164" y2="105" /><path d="M25 73Q60 89 94 78M154 78Q190 90 225 73M16 100Q50 116 84 105M164 105Q198 116 235 100" stroke="#86936f"/><line x1="76" y1="150" x2="174" y2="150" /></g><style>text{fill:#748263;stroke:none;font:8px ui-monospace,monospace;letter-spacing:1px}</style></svg>

substation.name: Substation
substation.definition: A substation is a grid facility containing equipment for switching, protection, control, and often voltage transformation. Some substations connect circuits without changing their voltage.
substation.caption: An equipment sketch showing a transformer, switching equipment, and supporting gantry; it is not a wiring diagram.
substation.svg: <svg viewBox="0 0 250 180" role="img" aria-label="An equipment sketch showing a transformer, switching equipment, and supporting gantry; it is not a wiring diagram." xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg"><g fill="none" stroke="#5d7450" stroke-width="1.4" stroke-linecap="round" stroke-linejoin="round"><path d="M25 151H225M34 151V37H215V151M27 37H222" /><path d="M59 37V62M119 37V62M185 37V62" /><path d="M54 51h10m-10 5h10m-10 5h10" /><circle cx="59" cy="65" r="3" /><path d="M114 51h10m-10 5h10m-10 5h10" /><circle cx="119" cy="65" r="3" /><path d="M180 51h10m-10 5h10m-10 5h10" /><circle cx="185" cy="65" r="3" /><path d="M59 68V89M119 68V89M185 68V96" /><rect x="40" y="89" width="98" height="51" rx="2" fill="#e4e9d7"/><line x1="51" y1="99" x2="51" y2="132" /><line x1="63" y1="99" x2="63" y2="132" /><line x1="75" y1="99" x2="75" y2="132" /><line x1="87" y1="99" x2="87" y2="132" /><line x1="99" y1="99" x2="99" y2="132" /><line x1="111" y1="99" x2="111" y2="132" /><line x1="123" y1="99" x2="123" y2="132" /><path d="M49 140V151M129 140V151" /><rect x="170" y="96" width="30" height="40" rx="2" fill="#e4e9d7"/><path d="M176 136V151M195 136V151M138 114H170" /></g><style>text{fill:#748263;stroke:none;font:8px ui-monospace,monospace;letter-spacing:1px}</style></svg>

distribution.name: Distribution
distribution.definition: Distribution networks carry electricity from substations to end users. They include medium-voltage feeders, local transformers, and the lower-voltage circuits serving homes and businesses.
distribution.caption: A simplified overhead connection: the medium-voltage line feeds the transformer; its low-voltage service drop reaches the building’s meter. Individual phases and neutral are omitted.
distribution.svg: <svg viewBox="0 0 250 180" role="img" aria-label="A simplified overhead connection: the medium-voltage line feeds the transformer; its low-voltage service drop reaches the building’s meter. Individual phases and neutral are omitted." xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg"><g fill="none" stroke="#5d7450" stroke-width="1.4" stroke-linecap="round" stroke-linejoin="round"><path d="M57 39V153M39 56H82M23 44H225" /><path d="M70 44V56M65 48H75M65 52H75" /><path d="M87 44Q108 50 90 66M90 66V76M85 69H95M85 73H95" /><rect x="70" y="76" width="38" height="41" rx="2" fill="#dce3c8"/><path d="M70 84H108M57 86H70M57 110H70M108 98Q156 116 209.2 95V126" /><g transform="translate(174 103) scale(0.8)"><path d="M0 25 25 5 50 25M6 21V57H44V21" /><rect x="22" y="37" width="10" height="20" rx="2" /><rect x="12" y="28" width="8" height="9" rx="2" /></g><rect x="204.2" y="126" width="10" height="10" rx="2" fill="#dce3c8"/><text x="23" y="29" >MEDIUM VOLTAGE</text><text x="126" y="82" >SERVICE DROP</text><circle cx="87" cy="44" r="2" fill="#5d7450"/></g><style>text{fill:#748263;stroke:none;font:8px ui-monospace,monospace;letter-spacing:1px}</style></svg>

inverter.name: Inverter
inverter.definition: An inverter converts direct-current electricity into alternating-current electricity. Grid-connected inverters also control how a resource interacts with the network.
inverter.caption: DC enters on the left; the inverter produces a controlled AC output on the right.
inverter.svg: <svg viewBox="0 0 250 180" role="img" aria-label="DC enters on the left; the inverter produces a controlled AC output on the right." xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg"><g fill="none" stroke="#5d7450" stroke-width="1.4" stroke-linecap="round" stroke-linejoin="round"><rect x="83" y="46" width="86" height="92" rx="2" fill="#e6eadc"/><rect x="97" y="60" width="58" height="31" rx="2" /><path d="M101 75h20m-20 5h20m7-3q6-12 12 0t12 0" /><circle cx="126" cy="115" r="5" stroke="#93a74d"/><path d="M34 76H83M34 91H83M169 76H216M169 91H216" /><text x="38" y="59" >DC</text><text x="194" y="59" >AC</text></g><style>text{fill:#748263;stroke:none;font:8px ui-monospace,monospace;letter-spacing:1px}</style></svg>

battery-storage.name: Battery storage
battery-storage.definition: A battery energy storage system converts electrical energy into chemical energy and back again. Its power rating and energy capacity describe different limits: how fast it can deliver electricity and how much it can store.
battery-storage.caption: Filled and unfilled cells suggest stored energy; the drawing is symbolic, not a specific battery chemistry.
battery-storage.svg: <svg viewBox="0 0 250 180" role="img" aria-label="Filled and unfilled cells suggest stored energy; the drawing is symbolic, not a specific battery chemistry." xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg"><g fill="none" stroke="#5d7450" stroke-width="1.4" stroke-linecap="round" stroke-linejoin="round"><rect x="65" y="53" width="117" height="78" rx="2" fill="#e5e9d9"/><rect x="182" y="77" width="9" height="30" rx="2" /><rect x="76" y="65" width="23" height="54" rx="2" fill="#afc078"/><rect x="108" y="65" width="23" height="54" rx="2" fill="#afc078"/><rect x="140" y="65" width="23" height="54" rx="2" stroke-dasharray="3 3"/><text x="78" y="153" >POWER + ENERGY</text></g><style>text{fill:#748263;stroke:none;font:8px ui-monospace,monospace;letter-spacing:1px}</style></svg>

frequency.name: Frequency
frequency.definition: Frequency is the number of AC cycles per second, measured in hertz. Grid operators work to keep it near its nominal value as electricity supply and demand change.
frequency.caption: The marked interval covers one complete cycle of the waveform. The sketch is not drawn to a time scale.

demand-response.name: Demand response
demand-response.definition: Demand response changes electricity consumption in response to prices, incentives, or instructions. It can reduce use, move it to another time, or adjust it to support grid operation.
demand-response.caption: A symbolic load profile: the solid line reduces a peak and moves some consumption to a later period. The dashed line shows the original profile.
demand-response.svg: <svg viewBox="0 0 250 180" role="img" aria-label="A symbolic load profile: the solid line reduces a peak and moves some consumption to a later period. The dashed line shows the original profile." xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg"><g fill="none" stroke="#5d7450" stroke-width="1.4" stroke-linecap="round" stroke-linejoin="round"><path d="M34 38V140H216" stroke="#a9b19c"/><path d="M35 117 70 117 93 65 136 65 157 117H213" stroke="#b1b69f" stroke-dasharray="4 4"/><path d="M35 117 70 117 93 92 136 92 157 117 180 92 204 92" stroke="#93a74d"/><path d="M109 69V87M105 82 109 88 113 82" /><text x="49" y="157" >SHIFT / REDUCE</text></g><style>text{fill:#748263;stroke:none;font:8px ui-monospace,monospace;letter-spacing:1px}</style></svg>

power-grid.name: Power grid
power-grid.definition: The electricity grid is an interconnected network of lines, substations, and other equipment that links electricity producers and users. Connected resources and operators work together to keep the system operating.
power-grid.caption: Nodes and connecting lines represent a network. This is a conceptual sketch, not a geographic map.
power-grid.svg: <svg viewBox="0 0 250 180" role="img" aria-label="Nodes and connecting lines represent a network. This is a conceptual sketch, not a geographic map." xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg"><g fill="none" stroke="#5d7450" stroke-width="1.4" stroke-linecap="round" stroke-linejoin="round"><line x1="48" y1="54" x2="119" y2="36" /><line x1="119" y1="36" x2="193" y2="65" /><line x1="48" y1="54" x2="84" y2="123" /><line x1="119" y1="36" x2="126" y2="96" /><line x1="193" y1="65" x2="126" y2="96" /><line x1="193" y1="65" x2="193" y2="139" /><line x1="126" y1="96" x2="84" y2="123" /><line x1="126" y1="96" x2="193" y2="139" /><circle cx="48" cy="54" r="8" fill="#e2e8ce"/><circle cx="119" cy="36" r="8" fill="#e2e8ce"/><circle cx="193" cy="65" r="8" fill="#e2e8ce"/><circle cx="84" cy="123" r="8" fill="#e2e8ce"/><circle cx="126" cy="96" r="8" fill="#e2e8ce"/><circle cx="193" cy="139" r="8" fill="#e2e8ce"/></g><style>text{fill:#748263;stroke:none;font:8px ui-monospace,monospace;letter-spacing:1px}</style></svg>

feeder.name: Feeder
feeder.definition: A distribution feeder is a circuit supplying electricity from a substation into a service area. It may branch into smaller circuits and connect loads, local generation, and storage.
feeder.caption: A source at the left supplies a branching circuit. Dots mark connection points; equipment details are omitted.
feeder.svg: <svg viewBox="0 0 250 180" role="img" aria-label="A source at the left supplies a branching circuit. Dots mark connection points; equipment details are omitted." xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg"><g fill="none" stroke="#5d7450" stroke-width="1.4" stroke-linecap="round" stroke-linejoin="round"><rect x="35" y="68" width="35" height="43" rx="2" fill="#e2e8ce"/><path d="M70 90H192M101 90V51H162M132 90V139H193" /><circle cx="101" cy="90" r="4" fill="#96a85c"/><circle cx="132" cy="90" r="4" fill="#96a85c"/><circle cx="162" cy="51" r="4" fill="#96a85c"/><circle cx="192" cy="90" r="4" fill="#96a85c"/><circle cx="193" cy="139" r="4" fill="#96a85c"/><text x="37" y="128" >SOURCE</text></g><style>text{fill:#748263;stroke:none;font:8px ui-monospace,monospace;letter-spacing:1px}</style></svg>

busbar.name: Busbar
busbar.definition: A busbar is a conductor, or set of conductors, that forms a common connection point. In a substation, it connects incoming and outgoing circuits through switching equipment.
busbar.caption: The thick horizontal conductor is the common bus; the vertical connections represent attached circuits.
busbar.svg: <svg viewBox="0 0 250 180" role="img" aria-label="The thick horizontal conductor is the common bus; the vertical connections represent attached circuits." xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg"><g fill="none" stroke="#5d7450" stroke-width="1.4" stroke-linecap="round" stroke-linejoin="round"><path d="M47 88H204" stroke-width="5"/><path d="M67 88V49M67 88V132" /><circle cx="67" cy="47" r="4" /><circle cx="67" cy="134" r="4" /><path d="M117 88V49M117 88V132" /><circle cx="117" cy="47" r="4" /><circle cx="117" cy="134" r="4" /><path d="M167 88V49M167 88V132" /><circle cx="167" cy="47" r="4" /><circle cx="167" cy="134" r="4" /><text x="91" y="159" >COMMON BUS</text></g><style>text{fill:#748263;stroke:none;font:8px ui-monospace,monospace;letter-spacing:1px}</style></svg>

circuit-breaker.name: Circuit breaker
circuit-breaker.definition: A circuit breaker can open a circuit carrying normal or fault current, within its interrupting ratings. Protection systems can command it to isolate a faulted part of the grid.
circuit-breaker.caption: An open breaker contact separates the two sides of a circuit. This is a schematic representation.
circuit-breaker.svg: <svg viewBox="0 0 250 180" role="img" aria-label="An open breaker contact separates the two sides of a circuit. This is a schematic representation." xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg"><g fill="none" stroke="#5d7450" stroke-width="1.4" stroke-linecap="round" stroke-linejoin="round"><path d="M28 96H85M163 96H220" /><rect x="85" y="59" width="78" height="76" rx="2" fill="#e4e8d9"/><circle cx="101" cy="96" r="4" /><circle cx="146" cy="96" r="4" /><line x1="104" y1="93" x2="142" y2="72" stroke="#93a74d"/><path d="M124 57V40M114 40H134" /><text x="95" y="156" >OPEN</text></g><style>text{fill:#748263;stroke:none;font:8px ui-monospace,monospace;letter-spacing:1px}</style></svg>

insulator.name: Insulator
insulator.definition: An insulator resists electric current and separates energized conductors from structures or other conductors. Overhead line insulators also carry mechanical loads.
insulator.caption: A simplified disc-style insulator string, shown without the conductor and tower attachments.
insulator.svg: <svg viewBox="0 0 250 180" role="img" aria-label="A simplified disc-style insulator string, shown without the conductor and tower attachments." xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg"><g fill="none" stroke="#5d7450" stroke-width="1.4" stroke-linecap="round" stroke-linejoin="round"><path d="M124 28V146M112 27H136M108 145H140" /><path d="M113 43Q124 36 135 43L145 51Q124 61 103 51Z" fill="#e4e9d7"/><path d="M113 59Q124 52 135 59L145 67Q124 77 103 67Z" fill="#e4e9d7"/><path d="M113 75Q124 68 135 75L145 83Q124 93 103 83Z" fill="#e4e9d7"/><path d="M113 91Q124 84 135 91L145 99Q124 109 103 99Z" fill="#e4e9d7"/><path d="M113 107Q124 100 135 107L145 115Q124 125 103 115Z" fill="#e4e9d7"/></g><style>text{fill:#748263;stroke:none;font:8px ui-monospace,monospace;letter-spacing:1px}</style></svg>

conductor.name: Conductor
conductor.definition: A conductor allows electric charge to move readily. Grid conductors are commonly made with aluminum or copper; some overhead conductors include a reinforcing core for strength.
conductor.caption: An overhead wire above and a separate end view below. The end view shows a simplified stranded construction.
conductor.svg: <svg viewBox="0 0 250 180" role="img" aria-label="An overhead wire above and a separate end view below. The end view shows a simplified stranded construction." xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg"><g fill="none" stroke="#5d7450" stroke-width="1.4" stroke-linecap="round" stroke-linejoin="round"><path d="M25 48Q116 94 222 49M25 55Q116 101 222 56M25 62Q116 108 222 63" /><circle cx="159" cy="133" r="25" fill="#e6eadc"/><circle cx="159" cy="133" r="5" /><circle cx="149" cy="127" r="5" /><circle cx="159" cy="121" r="5" /><circle cx="169" cy="127" r="5" /><circle cx="149" cy="139" r="5" /><circle cx="159" cy="145" r="5" /><circle cx="169" cy="139" r="5" /><text x="28" y="131" >STRANDED</text><text x="28" y="143" >WIRE</text><text x="195" y="136" >END VIEW</text></g><style>text{fill:#748263;stroke:none;font:8px ui-monospace,monospace;letter-spacing:1px}</style></svg>

voltage.name: Voltage
voltage.definition: Voltage measures electrical potential difference, in volts. Grid equipment operates at specified voltage levels, which are changed by transformers as power moves through the network.
voltage.caption: A symbolic voltmeter connected across two terminals measures their potential difference.
voltage.svg: <svg viewBox="0 0 250 180" role="img" aria-label="A symbolic voltmeter connected across two terminals measures their potential difference." xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg"><g fill="none" stroke="#5d7450" stroke-width="1.4" stroke-linecap="round" stroke-linejoin="round"><rect x="69" y="57" width="110" height="70" rx="2" /><circle cx="124" cy="90" r="24" /><text x="124" y="90" text-anchor="middle" dominant-baseline="central" style="font-size:23px;letter-spacing:0">V</text><path d="M69 92H39V137H97M179 92H209V137H151" /><circle cx="101" cy="137" r="4" /><circle cx="147" cy="137" r="4" /><text x="124" y="159" text-anchor="middle">POTENTIAL DIFFERENCE</text></g><style>text{fill:#748263;stroke:none;font:8px ui-monospace,monospace;letter-spacing:1px}</style></svg>

current.name: Current
current.definition: Electric current is the rate of flow of electric charge, measured in amperes. In ordinary grid conductors it produces resistive heating, so equipment has current ratings for specified operating conditions.
current.caption: Dots and arrows represent conventional charge flow in one direction. AC reverses direction during each cycle.
current.svg: <svg viewBox="0 0 250 180" role="img" aria-label="Dots and arrows represent conventional charge flow in one direction. AC reverses direction during each cycle." xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg"><g fill="none" stroke="#5d7450" stroke-width="1.4" stroke-linecap="round" stroke-linejoin="round"><path d="M30 71H216M30 111H216" /><circle cx="62" cy="91" r="5" fill="#aabb71"/><path d="M49 91h-10m8-4 5 4-5 4" stroke="#93a74d"/><circle cx="109" cy="91" r="5" fill="#aabb71"/><path d="M96 91h-10m8-4 5 4-5 4" stroke="#93a74d"/><circle cx="156" cy="91" r="5" fill="#aabb71"/><path d="M143 91h-10m8-4 5 4-5 4" stroke="#93a74d"/><circle cx="200" cy="91" r="5" fill="#aabb71"/><path d="M187 91h-10m8-4 5 4-5 4" stroke="#93a74d"/><text x="86" y="141" >CHARGE FLOW →</text></g><style>text{fill:#748263;stroke:none;font:8px ui-monospace,monospace;letter-spacing:1px}</style></svg>

power.name: Power
power.definition: Power is the rate of energy transfer. Real electrical power is measured in watts; kilowatts and megawatts are common units for equipment and grid-scale resources.
power.caption: A constant 2 kW rate is shown as a horizontal line; energy depends on how long that rate lasts.
power.svg: <svg viewBox="0 0 250 180" role="img" aria-label="A constant 2 kW rate is shown as a horizontal line; energy depends on how long that rate lasts." xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg"><g fill="none" stroke="#5d7450" stroke-width="1.4" stroke-linecap="round" stroke-linejoin="round"><path d="M34 38V140H216" stroke="#a9b19c"/><path d="M35 80H214" stroke="#93a74d"/><text x="52" y="68" >2 kW</text><text x="158" y="158" >TIME →</text></g><style>text{fill:#748263;stroke:none;font:8px ui-monospace,monospace;letter-spacing:1px}</style></svg>

energy.name: Energy
energy.definition: Electrical energy is accumulated power over time. Electricity bills commonly measure it in kilowatt-hours, while grid-scale generation and storage often use megawatt-hours.
energy.caption: The shaded area represents 6 kWh: a constant 2 kW over three hours.
energy.svg: <svg viewBox="0 0 250 180" role="img" aria-label="The shaded area represents 6 kWh: a constant 2 kW over three hours." xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg"><g fill="none" stroke="#5d7450" stroke-width="1.4" stroke-linecap="round" stroke-linejoin="round"><path d="M34 38V140H216" stroke="#a9b19c"/><path d="M35 140V78H212V140Z" fill="#d6e0b7" stroke="none"/><path d="M35 78H212" stroke="#93a74d"/><text x="82" y="111" >6 kWh</text><text x="76" y="159" >2 kW × 3 h</text></g><style>text{fill:#748263;stroke:none;font:8px ui-monospace,monospace;letter-spacing:1px}</style></svg>

alternating-current.name: Alternating current
alternating-current.definition: Alternating current changes direction periodically. Most transmission and distribution networks use AC, allowing transformers to change voltage and connecting many resources to a shared electrical frequency.
alternating-current.caption: An ideal alternating waveform crosses the zero line as it reverses sign.

three-phase-power.name: Three-phase power
three-phase-power.definition: A balanced three-phase supply has three sinusoidal voltages of the same frequency and magnitude, separated by one-third of a cycle, or 120 degrees. Three-phase systems are widely used for generation, transmission, and large electrical loads.
three-phase-power.caption: Three balanced sinusoidal waveforms, separated by one-third of a cycle.

generator.name: Generator
generator.definition: A rotating generator converts mechanical energy into electrical energy through electromagnetic induction. A turbine or another prime mover supplies the mechanical input.
generator.caption: A conceptual cross-section: the magnetic rotor turns within the wound stator, driven by a shaft. Real winding and pole arrangements vary.
generator.svg: <svg viewBox="0 0 250 180" role="img" aria-label="A conceptual cross-section: the magnetic rotor turns within the wound stator, driven by a shaft. Real winding and pole arrangements vary." xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg"><g fill="none" stroke="#5d7450" stroke-width="1.4" stroke-linecap="round" stroke-linejoin="round"><circle cx="125" cy="92" r="45" fill="#e4e9d5"/><circle cx="125" cy="92" r="32" /><g transform="rotate(0 125 92)"><rect x="119" y="51" width="12" height="12" rx="2" fill="#b9c88e"/></g><g transform="rotate(45 125 92)"><rect x="119" y="51" width="12" height="12" rx="2" fill="#b9c88e"/></g><g transform="rotate(90 125 92)"><rect x="119" y="51" width="12" height="12" rx="2" fill="#b9c88e"/></g><g transform="rotate(135 125 92)"><rect x="119" y="51" width="12" height="12" rx="2" fill="#b9c88e"/></g><g transform="rotate(180 125 92)"><rect x="119" y="51" width="12" height="12" rx="2" fill="#b9c88e"/></g><g transform="rotate(225 125 92)"><rect x="119" y="51" width="12" height="12" rx="2" fill="#b9c88e"/></g><g transform="rotate(270 125 92)"><rect x="119" y="51" width="12" height="12" rx="2" fill="#b9c88e"/></g><g transform="rotate(315 125 92)"><rect x="119" y="51" width="12" height="12" rx="2" fill="#b9c88e"/></g><path d="M25 92H94M156 85H219M156 99H219" /><rect x="106" y="79" width="38" height="26" rx="2" fill="#c9d7a8" transform="rotate(-30 125 92)"/><text x="112" y="98" style="font-size:9px;letter-spacing:0">N</text><text x="133" y="88" style="font-size:9px;letter-spacing:0">S</text><path d="M125 46V30H166M137 96L181 128H190" /><text x="169" y="33" >STATOR</text><text x="192" y="131" >ROTOR</text><text x="24" y="77" >SHAFT</text><text x="182" y="70" >AC OUT</text></g><style>text{fill:#748263;stroke:none;font:8px ui-monospace,monospace;letter-spacing:1px}</style></svg>

solar-photovoltaic.name: Solar photovoltaic
solar-photovoltaic.definition: Photovoltaic cells convert light into direct-current electricity. Modules combine cells, and an inverter typically connects their output to an AC network.
solar-photovoltaic.caption: A tilted array of photovoltaic modules. The sketch represents a physical installation, not a wiring diagram.

wind-turbine.name: Wind turbine
wind-turbine.definition: A wind turbine extracts energy from moving air using a rotor. The rotor drives a generator, and electrical equipment conditions the output for connection to the grid.
wind-turbine.caption: A three-bladed horizontal-axis turbine: rotor, nacelle, and tower.
wind-turbine.svg: <svg viewBox="0 0 250 180" role="img" aria-label="A three-bladed horizontal-axis turbine: rotor, nacelle, and tower." xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg"><g fill="none" stroke="#5d7450" stroke-width="1.4" stroke-linecap="round" stroke-linejoin="round"><path d="M119 82 114 149H132L126 82M123 71 128 25Q119 17 117 32L119 69M115 77 76 100Q72 110 84 105L120 82M129 77 165 103Q176 105 168 96L130 72" /><circle cx="123" cy="76" r="7" fill="#d7dfbd"/><line x1="88" y1="150" x2="157" y2="150" /></g><style>text{fill:#748263;stroke:none;font:8px ui-monospace,monospace;letter-spacing:1px}</style></svg>

capacity-factor.name: Capacity factor
capacity-factor.definition: Capacity factor is energy produced over a period divided by the energy that would be produced at continuous rated power over that same period. It reflects resource availability, operation, and outages.
capacity-factor.caption: The filled quarter represents 25% of a full-output reference. This is an area comparison, not a time series.
capacity-factor.svg: <svg viewBox="0 0 250 180" role="img" aria-label="The filled quarter represents 25% of a full-output reference. This is an area comparison, not a time series." xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg"><g fill="none" stroke="#5d7450" stroke-width="1.4" stroke-linecap="round" stroke-linejoin="round"><rect x="49" y="43" width="153" height="95" rx="2" stroke-dasharray="4 4"/><rect x="49" y="114" width="153" height="24" rx="2" fill="#b3c77f"/><text x="84" y="94" >25%</text><text x="51" y="158" >ACTUAL / POSSIBLE</text></g><style>text{fill:#748263;stroke:none;font:8px ui-monospace,monospace;letter-spacing:1px}</style></svg>

storage-duration.name: Storage duration
storage-duration.definition: Storage duration is how long a fully charged system can deliver a stated discharge power. Nominal duration is usable energy capacity divided by that power, with both ratings measured on the same AC or DC basis.
storage-duration.caption: A battery beside a clock represents the energy-to-power ratio, not a particular operating schedule.
storage-duration.svg: <svg viewBox="0 0 250 180" role="img" aria-label="A battery beside a clock represents the energy-to-power ratio, not a particular operating schedule." xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg"><g fill="none" stroke="#5d7450" stroke-width="1.4" stroke-linecap="round" stroke-linejoin="round"><rect x="40" y="54" width="54" height="72" rx="2" fill="#e3e8d6"/><rect x="57" y="46" width="20" height="8" rx="2" /><path d="M53 89H81M67 76V103" /><circle cx="162" cy="91" r="38" /><path d="M162 61V91H186" /><text x="119" y="151" >ENERGY ÷ POWER</text></g><style>text{fill:#748263;stroke:none;font:8px ui-monospace,monospace;letter-spacing:1px}</style></svg>

microgrid.name: Microgrid
microgrid.definition: A microgrid is a group of connected loads and distributed energy resources within a defined electrical boundary, controlled as one system and able to operate independently. A grid-connected microgrid can disconnect from the wider grid to run in island mode.
microgrid.caption: The dashed boundary encloses local generation, storage, and a building. The open switch represents separation from the external grid.
microgrid.svg: <svg viewBox="0 0 250 180" role="img" aria-label="The dashed boundary encloses local generation, storage, and a building. The open switch represents separation from the external grid." xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg"><g fill="none" stroke="#5d7450" stroke-width="1.4" stroke-linecap="round" stroke-linejoin="round"><rect x="33" y="34" width="182" height="119" rx="2" stroke-dasharray="5 4"/><g transform="translate(100 78) scale(0.85)"><path d="M0 25 25 5 50 25M6 21V57H44V21" /><rect x="22" y="37" width="10" height="20" rx="2" /><rect x="12" y="28" width="8" height="9" rx="2" /></g><rect x="49" y="105" width="28" height="30" rx="2" fill="#dce6c1"/><path d="M46 64H89L83 87H40ZM61 64 55 87M44 76H86M62 87V105M77 119H106M143 119H191V73M191 73H217M223 67 236 56M223 73H242" /><circle cx="220" cy="73" r="3" /></g><style>text{fill:#748263;stroke:none;font:8px ui-monospace,monospace;letter-spacing:1px}</style></svg>

load.name: Load
load.definition: Load means electrical demand, or the equipment consuming electrical power. System load changes throughout the day as people, businesses, and machines change their activities.
load.caption: An incoming connection supplies a building. The sketch symbolizes demand, rather than showing a complete electrical circuit.
load.svg: <svg viewBox="0 0 250 180" role="img" aria-label="An incoming connection supplies a building. The sketch symbolizes demand, rather than showing a complete electrical circuit." xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg"><g fill="none" stroke="#5d7450" stroke-width="1.4" stroke-linecap="round" stroke-linejoin="round"><g transform="translate(76 66) scale(1.3)"><path d="M0 25 25 5 50 25M6 21V57H44V21" /><rect x="22" y="37" width="10" height="20" rx="2" /><rect x="12" y="28" width="8" height="9" rx="2" /></g><path d="M28 102H79M39 94 49 102 39 110" stroke="#93a74d"/><text x="84" y="162" >ELECTRICITY IN</text></g><style>text{fill:#748263;stroke:none;font:8px ui-monospace,monospace;letter-spacing:1px}</style></svg>

peak-demand.name: Peak demand
peak-demand.definition: Peak demand is the maximum electrical demand measured or forecast over a stated time interval and period. Networks and resources must be planned to serve high-demand conditions reliably.
peak-demand.caption: A point marks the maximum on an illustrative daily demand curve. No real measurements are shown.
peak-demand.svg: <svg viewBox="0 0 250 180" role="img" aria-label="A point marks the maximum on an illustrative daily demand curve. No real measurements are shown." xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg"><g fill="none" stroke="#5d7450" stroke-width="1.4" stroke-linecap="round" stroke-linejoin="round"><path d="M34 38V140H216" stroke="#a9b19c"/><path d="M35 121C53 122 55 131 71 119S90 70 107 75 124 100 141 81 160 45 177 59 194 99 214 105" stroke="#93a74d"/><circle cx="169" cy="56" r="6" fill="#c4d58b"/><path d="M169 49V26M169 140V66" stroke-dasharray="3 4"/><text x="145" y="20" >PEAK</text></g><style>text{fill:#748263;stroke:none;font:8px ui-monospace,monospace;letter-spacing:1px}</style></svg>

dispatch.name: Dispatch
dispatch.definition: Dispatch assigns operating levels to available resources to meet demand while respecting system constraints. It can consider costs, equipment limits, network conditions, and reliability requirements.
dispatch.caption: Three adjustable output levels symbolize resource setpoints. They are not a real dispatch schedule.
dispatch.svg: <svg viewBox="0 0 250 180" role="img" aria-label="Three adjustable output levels symbolize resource setpoints. They are not a real dispatch schedule." xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg"><g fill="none" stroke="#5d7450" stroke-width="1.4" stroke-linecap="round" stroke-linejoin="round"><rect x="54" y="42" width="23" height="86" rx="2" /><rect x="48" y="68" width="35" height="11" rx="2" fill="#bdcd8a"/><rect x="117" y="42" width="23" height="86" rx="2" /><rect x="111" y="85" width="35" height="11" rx="2" fill="#bdcd8a"/><rect x="180" y="42" width="23" height="86" rx="2" /><rect x="174" y="102" width="35" height="11" rx="2" fill="#bdcd8a"/><text x="58" y="155" >RESOURCE OUTPUT</text></g><style>text{fill:#748263;stroke:none;font:8px ui-monospace,monospace;letter-spacing:1px}</style></svg>

load-curve.name: Load curve
load-curve.definition: A load curve plots electrical power demand against time. It shows how demand changes through a day or another period. This time profile is different from an economic demand curve, which relates demand to price.
load-curve.caption: An illustrative daily load profile. The shape is conceptual; no site or measured day is represented.
load-curve.svg: <svg viewBox="0 0 250 180" role="img" aria-label="An illustrative daily load profile. The shape is conceptual; no site or measured day is represented." xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg"><g fill="none" stroke="#5d7450" stroke-width="1.4" stroke-linecap="round" stroke-linejoin="round"><path d="M34 38V140H216" stroke="#a9b19c"/><path d="M35 121C53 122 55 131 71 119S90 70 107 75 124 100 141 81 160 45 177 59 194 99 214 105" stroke="#93a74d"/><text x="36" y="158" >00:00</text><text x="169" y="158" >24:00</text></g><style>text{fill:#748263;stroke:none;font:8px ui-monospace,monospace;letter-spacing:1px}</style></svg>

pumped-hydro-storage.name: Pumped hydro storage
pumped-hydro-storage.definition: Pumped hydro storage uses electricity to pump water to a higher reservoir. Water later flows back through a turbine to generate electricity, returning part of the energy used to pump it.
pumped-hydro-storage.caption: Upper and lower reservoirs connect through a pump/turbine. The downhill arrow shows generating flow; the uphill arrow shows pumping flow.
pumped-hydro-storage.svg: <svg viewBox="0 0 250 180" role="img" aria-label="Upper and lower reservoirs connect through a pump/turbine. The downhill arrow shows generating flow; the uphill arrow shows pumping flow." xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg"><g fill="none" stroke="#5d7450" stroke-width="1.4" stroke-linecap="round" stroke-linejoin="round"><path d="M143 43V70H209V43M143 55H209" fill="#dbe3c5"/><path d="M28 120V146H91V120M28 131H91" fill="#dbe3c5"/><path d="M163 70 118 132H91M171 70 124 138H91" /><circle cx="120" cy="135" r="10" fill="#edf0e4"/><path d="M120 125V145M110 135H130" /><defs><marker id="hydro-down" viewBox="0 0 8 8" refX="7" refY="4" markerWidth="7" markerHeight="7" orient="auto"><path d="M1 1 7 4 1 7" fill="none" stroke="#93a74d" stroke-width="1.2"/></marker><marker id="hydro-up" viewBox="0 0 8 8" refX="7" refY="4" markerWidth="7" markerHeight="7" orient="auto"><path d="M1 1 7 4 1 7" fill="none" stroke="#5d7450" stroke-width="1.2"/></marker></defs><line x1="190" y1="84" x2="166" y2="116" stroke="#93a74d" marker-end="url(#hydro-down)"/><line x1="105" y1="109" x2="126" y2="80" marker-end="url(#hydro-up)"/><text x="173" y="31" >UPPER</text><text x="29" y="111" >LOWER</text><text x="143" y="164" >PUMP / TURBINE</text></g><style>text{fill:#748263;stroke:none;font:8px ui-monospace,monospace;letter-spacing:1px}</style></svg>

underground-cable.name: Underground cable
underground-cable.definition: An underground power cable has conductors enclosed in electrical insulation and protective layers. It may be installed directly in the ground, in ducts, or in tunnels.
underground-cable.caption: A conceptual three-core cable beneath a ground surface. The layer arrangement is illustrative, not a specification.
underground-cable.svg: <svg viewBox="0 0 250 180" role="img" aria-label="A conceptual three-core cable beneath a ground surface.
